gluten-free.title: Gluten Free
gluten-free.what: What we can serve gluten free, and how it has to be handled to mean anything. Read the protocol before the menu — the menu is the easy half.

items: Ask the guest outright: is this a preference, or an allergy? Everything below depends on the answer.
PREFERENCE — build it off the gluten free menu and send it like any other ticket.
ALLERGY — the kit comes out, gloves change in front of the guest, and one person owns that plate from the pull to the pass.
Ring it on the screen so the kitchen sees ALLERGY, not a note buried in the modifiers.
Tell the MOD. The ServSafe manager on duty owns every allergy ticket that goes out.
We can accommodate gluten free. We cannot guarantee a gluten free kitchen — there is flour in the air and shared equipment on every line.
Never say "it's gluten free" about a dish. Say what we do: gluten free bun, clean board, fresh gloves, separate utensils.
NOTHING FRIED. We cannot say what has been through a fryer, so no fries, no tenders, no wings, no fried anything.
Caesar Salad comes with NO croutons. Hamburger Steak comes with NO gravy and NO toast.
Mugshakes only in vanilla, chocolate, strawberry and peanut butter — no Monster Cookie.
If you are not certain about an item, ask the MOD before you say it to the table.

days.focus: How an allergy ticket is built
items: The kit lives in one place and stays together: its own coloured knife, its own cutting board, Udi's buns single wrapped.
Fresh gloves, changed in front of the guest.
Clean surface before anything touches it. Wipe down and sanitise the area you are building on.
One person carries the plate down the line. Do not hand it off.
No reused knives on the way down — a clean knife is worth the extra ten seconds.
Udi's bun stays wrapped until the moment it is dressed.
